title: Computability
summary: Computability asks which input-output tasks can be carried out by an idealized finite procedure.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared theory of computation context is fixed.

content.plain: Computability asks which input-output tasks can be carried out by an idealized finite procedure.
content.exact: A partial function is computable when some accepted model of effective computation computes it; standard models agree on the classical computable functions.
content.example: Integer addition is computable; the halting problem is undecidable.
content.caveat: Computability ignores practical resource bounds unless complexity is added.
